# Results — Study 402 (Engulfing Pattern)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a bullish
engulfing candle marks a bottom and the next day(s) rise; a bearish engulfing marks a top and the
next day(s) fall** — tested as a clean event study on a fixed **30-name** basket (29 liquid US
large-caps + **SPY**). We detect every engulfing candle by the precise real-body OHLC rule, enter
the **next** open (one execution lag), and measure the forward **1 / 3 / 5 / 10-day** return
**signed by the pattern direction** (long after bullish, short after bearish), against the
unconditional base rate. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV, `auto_adjust=True` (total-return adjusted) — 29 long-listed US large-caps + SPY (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-06-18** (last bar; pulled 2026-06-21) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-18 (**21.5** years; 5,399 bars per name) |
| Fingerprint | `bf1d6cb7ca54` (sha1[:12] of basket closes) |
| Events | **12,144** engulfing candles (5,736 bullish · 6,408 bearish) at H=1 |
| Detector / entry / costs | real-body engulfing (opposite colours, larger engulfing body); enter the **next open**, exit close +H; **5 bps** one-way × 2 (round trip) + **50 bps/yr** borrow on the short (bearish) leg |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The basket is 30 names *still trading* in 2026. A
> fixed surviving-names panel cannot include firms delisted after a bad run, which mildly tilts the
> long (bullish) leg up. Crucially this bias works **against** our finding: it would *help* the
> bullish-reversal claim, yet the pattern still anti-predicts — so survivorship cannot explain the
> result away.

## The signal — signed forward return after every engulfing (long bullish / short bearish)

The signed-return mean is tested against **zero** with a Newey-West **HAC t** (the inference-bar
number) and a plain one-sample *t*; `baseL%` is the unconditional long forward return over the same
bars (the always-up drift the bullish leg must beat); the placebo *p* is the share of 10,000
random-bar / coin-sign draws whose mean **beats** the observed one.

| horizon | n events | bull | bear | signed mean | base (long) | win-rate | HAC *t* | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* | net |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 12,144 | 5,736 | 6,408 | **−0.049%** | +0.028% | 48.1% | **−3.79** | −3.89 | 1.000 | −0.150% |
| 3-day  | 12,143 | 5,736 | 6,407 | **−0.114%** | +0.141% | 48.2% | **−5.14** | −4.85 | 1.000 | −0.217% |
| 5-day  | 12,140 | 5,735 | 6,405 | **−0.174%** | +0.253% | 48.2% | **−5.74** | −5.61 | 1.000 | −0.279% |
| 10-day | 12,127 | 5,730 | 6,397 | **−0.176%** | +0.530% | 48.3% | **−4.25** | −4.08 | 1.000 | −0.285% |

Read it carefully. The signed engulfing return is **significantly negative at every horizon**
(HAC *t* from −3.79 to −5.74) — the pattern doesn't fail to predict the reversal, it **predicts the
opposite**. The win-rate is **below 50%** (48.1–48.3%), and the placebo *p* = 1.000 means *every*
random pick of the same many trades beats the engulfing mean. The textbook reversal is backwards on
this tape.

## Where the damage comes from — the bearish leg

Splitting the signed return by leg is the whole story:

| horizon | bullish leg mean | HAC *t* | win% | bearish leg mean | HAC *t* | win% |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | −0.011% | −0.59 | 49.7% | −0.083% | −4.55 | 46.7% |
| 3-day  | +0.072% | +2.24 | 52.1% | −0.281% | −8.76 | 44.7% |
| 5-day  | +0.130% | +2.92 | 53.5% | −0.446% | −10.46 | 43.6% |
| 10-day | +0.456% | +6.90 | 55.9% | −0.741% | −11.92 | 41.6% |

The **bearish** engulfing is the killer: after it, stocks keep **going up** (the short loses badly,
HAC *t* down to −11.92 at 10 days). The **bullish** leg looks positive over 3–10 days — but that is
just the market's always-up drift: the unconditional long return at 10 days is **+0.53%**, and the
bullish leg earns only **+0.46%**, i.e. it **underperforms simply holding for a day**. There is no
reversal alpha in either leg; the bullish leg rides beta and the bearish leg fights it.

## Costs — they only deepen a hole that's already below zero

Each event is a fresh round trip: **5 bps one-way × 2** (in + out) plus **50 bps/yr** borrow on the
short share. The gross signed mean is already negative at every horizon, so costs simply make it
worse (net −0.150% to −0.285%). There is nothing to charge against.

## Myth check — does a trend / volume filter rescue the reversal? No.

The textbook says the engulfing is most reliable **after a trend** and **on heavy volume**. We add
each filter (bullish needs a prior 10-day downtrend; bearish a prior uptrend; volume > 1.5× its
20-day average) at H=1:

| filter | n events | signed mean | HAC *t* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| plain | 12,144 | −0.049% | −3.79 | 48.1% |
| + downtrend/uptrend | 5,124 | −0.052% | −2.73 | 47.6% |
| + volume spike | 975 | −0.110% | −1.91 | 47.4% |
| + both | 405 | −0.135% | −1.40 | 47.9% |

Every filtered variant is **still negative** (the sub-2 *t*'s on the filtered cuts are just the
small samples, not a sign flip — the means and win-rates stay below zero / below 50%). The folk
"only count it after a trend, on volume" caveat does not turn the reversal positive; it just throws
away events.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic panel where we **plant** a known day-after reversal (the day after a detected
engulfing gets an extra drift in the pattern's direction), the inference behaves exactly as it must:

| planted edge | events | signed mean | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.000** (no edge) | 16,295 | +0.009% | +0.90 | 0.188 | 50% |
| **+0.004** (planted reversal) | 15,263 | +0.400% | **+38.77** | 0.000 | 62% |

With **no** planted reversal the test sits at *t* ≈ 0.9 (it does not manufacture significance from a
random walk); a planted reversal lights up to *t* = 38.77 with a 62% win-rate. The harness **can**
detect a real day-after reversal — the real tape simply doesn't have one (it has the opposite).

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The signed engulfing return is **significantly negative** at every horizon on
  the real tape (HAC *t* −3.79 to −5.74), the win-rate is **below 50%**, and the placebo *p* = 1.000.
  Far from clearing the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar *for the reversal*, the effect points the wrong way:
  there is no predictive reversal here. (The bullish leg's positive 3–10-day return is pure beta —
  it underperforms the unconditional long drift.) Survivorship works *for* the claim and still can't
  save it. **NONE.**
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The gross edge is negative before a cent of cost, so there is nothing to
  trade long-short; costs (round trip + borrow) only widen the loss to −0.15% to −0.29% per event.
  No capacity question even arises. **MIRAGE.**
- **A reliable reversal? — BUSTED.** The most-taught reversal pattern does not mark turns on liquid
  US large-caps: the bearish leg keeps rising and the bullish leg merely rides the market. Adding the
  textbook trend/volume filters doesn't flip it. The synthetic control proves the test *would* see a
  real reversal if one existed — so the negative finding is the genuine article, not a dead harness.
